image_description: A close-up portrait of a male Mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The subject features a characteristic iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a yellow bill, and mottled brown/grey chest plumage. The background consists of rippling water with soft focus, and a partial view of another duck is visible in the upper left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a distinct yellow coloration consistent with a male Mallard.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, contrasting with the green head feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, layered feather texture typical of waterproof plumage, and the posture suggests buoyancy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the Mallard description: iridescent green head, clear white neck ring, and brownish-grey chest/body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water; legs and feet are submerged or occluded by the body angle and cannot be visually verified.
The wings are folded against the body and largely occluded by the camera angle and crop; only the shoulder/chest area is clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail section is outside the frame or heavily obscured by the angle of the shot.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard drake) and rule out hybrid or nonsensical bird features.
To detect subtle texture anomalies in the feathers or unnatural blending at the waterline, which are common AI artifacts.
To ensure the white neck ring is a continuous, clean boundary and not bleeding into the green head or brown chest.
To verify that the water ripples have consistent geometry and the background duck does not exhibit structural melting.

Bill structure and connection to face

Also, inspect the eye for realistic specular highlights; dead or plastic-looking eyes are a sign of low-quality generation. Verify that the background duck, though blurry, maintains a plausible avian shape.
